# Synthetic Note C: Conditions for Calibration Comparisons

SYNTHETIC TEST FIXTURE — not a real publication. Author: Test Group C. Year and DOI not supplied. Paper type: theoretical note.

## Abstract

This note defines a conditional comparison rule. It contains no new empirical observations and does not estimate an effect size.

## Definitions

Let score M(c, d) be the value for configuration c in domain d under a specified metric. Define a within-domain improvement as M(adaptive, d) greater than M(baseline, d).

## Assumptions

The comparison uses the same domain, evaluation cases and metric for both configurations. No assumption states that the ordering is invariant across domains or metrics.

## Argument

An inequality in domain d1 does not logically imply the same inequality in domain d2 without an additional connecting premise. As a countermodel, assign adaptive 0.8 and baseline 0.7 in d1, but adaptive 0.6 and baseline 0.7 in d2. Both assignments satisfy the definitions.

## Conclusion

Within-domain improvements alone do not prove domain-independent superiority. This is a statement about the specified logical premises, not evidence of any empirical mechanism.

## Limits

The note does not supply a predictive model for which domain favors adaptation. It does not establish the distribution of effects in an actual research field.
